output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs comes mainly from inside the DC, not from Haverlow. Haverlow's trailer sensors show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open. The trailers were unloaded by about 23:00–23:40, but the receipt probe readings were keyed at 02:30–03:20. In between, pallets sat on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Since the night receiving team went from six to four in week 31, night dock-to-chamber time rose from 44 minutes to almost 4 hours. The night write-off rate went from 0.6% to 2.9%, and it is the same for Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label. Day shift is unchanged. The chambers held temperature. So the warm "receiving temperatures" mostly reflect dock dwell, and a chargeback and volume move against Haverlow would punish the wrong party. Next: restore night receiving capacity, or otherwise get chilled pallets into the chambers quickly. Set a maximum dock-to-chamber time and track it weekly from scan data. Do not drop the probe. Separately, sample Corriebank's claims against lots and receiving shift before changing credit terms. The cause of the DC-stage rise is well established. How much of the credit rise is over-claiming is still open.
